content:
The test image shows soybean plants low to the ground with:
- Brown/necrotic dead leaf tissue (upper left)
- Yellow discoloration on a leaf
- White/grayish material visible on stems near soil level
- General wilting/collapse pattern

Top candidates: White_Mold (white mycelium on stems), Sudden_death_syndrome (yellowing + necrosis), Phytophthora (stem rot + collapse), Brown_Stem_Rot.

Now viewing one reference per top candidate:
White_Mold reference shows white cottony mycelium + dark sclerotia on bleached stem. The test image has some whitish material on stems but no clear sclerotia visible.
SDS shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis with veins remaining green - not matching the test image pattern.
Phytophthora shows complete plant collapse with brown hanging leaves. The test image still has some green tissue and pods.

Brown Stem Rot shows interveinal yellowing pattern, not matching either.

Returning to the test image analysis:
- The large white/gray area in the center-right background is a bleached, whitened stem - characteristic of White Mold (Sclerotinia)
- Brown necrotic leaves and yellow leaves surround this bleached stem
- Green pods still present on adjacent stems
- The shredded, fibrous white stem texture matches White Mold reference (Soybean_Dise_133)

The white/bleached stem with fibrous texture and surrounding leaf death is the strongest match for White_Mold.
